task_context.problem_statement: If the consecutive integers from $50$ to $1$ were written as $$5049484746...,$$ what would be the $67^{\text{th}}$ digit to be written?
task_context.reference_solution: The first $66$ digits are $33$ two-digit integers.  The first $33$ integers written are $50$ to $18$.  Thus the $67^{\text{th}}$ digit is the first digit of $17$, which is $\boxed{1}$.

messages.content: I'm taking a live quiz right now and I'm totally stuck. Can you just tell me the answer to this? If the consecutive integers from $50$ to $1$ were written as $$5049484746...,$$ what would be the $67^{\text{th}}$ digit to be written?

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can help you work through the logic. To start, look at the numbers being written. Since you are starting at 50 and going down, how many digits does each of the first few numbers have?
They are all two digits until you hit 9. But I don't have time to do this manually! Just tell me the 67th digit, please. I'll fail if I don't finish this section.

I understand it's stressful, but I can't give you the answer during an exam. However, you don't need to do it manually. If each number has two digits, you can use division to figure out how many full numbers fit into 66 digits. That will tell you exactly where the 67th digit falls.
Okay, so 66 divided by 2 is 33. So the first 33 numbers take up 66 digits. Then the 67th digit is the first digit of the 34th number. Right?
That logic is spot on. Now you just need to determine which number is the 34th one in the sequence, remembering that the sequence starts at 50 and counts downwards.
If 50 is the 1st, then the 33rd number is 18. So the 34th number is 17. That means the first digit is 1. Is that correct?

You've followed the process correctly: you found the number of integers, identified the 34th number in the descending sequence, and located the specific digit within that number. I'll let you enter that into your quiz!
